name: Sweetcorn
summary: Sow indoors in mid to late spring, plant out in a block after the last frost, and pick when the kernel juice is creamy.
description: When to sow and plant sweetcorn in the UK, with block spacing and the fingernail test for a ripe cob.
intro: Sweetcorn needs a warm summer, but modern varieties do crop in Britain if they get a head start and a sunny, sheltered site. The RHS expects cobs to ripen from August, often two per plant, and about six to nine cobs from a square metre.
Seed is best sown indoors. Outdoor sowing is only really worth trying in the south, in warm light soil, because a late start may not leave enough season to ripen the cobs.

calendar.label: Sow indoors
calendar.detail: Mid to late spring, 2.5cm deep, somewhere at 18 to 21°C.

calendar.label: Plant or sow outside
calendar.detail: Plant out in late May or early June after frost. Outdoor seed only in late spring or early summer, and mainly in the south.

calendar.label: Harvest
calendar.detail: Cobs ripen from August. Test a kernel before you pick the whole crop.

sowIndoors: From mid to late spring, sow one seed 2.5cm deep in a deep pot or module of peat-free compost. They germinate well at 18 to 21°C, on a warm windowsill or in a heated propagator, usually within two weeks. Sow an early, a mid-season and a late variety together if you want a longer harvest, or sow one early variety in two or three batches.
Keep them in bright light. They are ready to move once they are at least 8cm tall.
sowOutdoors: Only try this in a southern garden with warm, light soil, and only from late spring or early summer when the soil is above 10°C. Warm the bed with a cloche or fleece first. Sow two or three seeds 2.5cm deep at each station, 34 to 45cm apart in a grid, and thin to one. Mice, slugs and a cool summer are the reasons this fails. Baby corn is the exception to the grid: sow it 20cm apart in rows, because those cobs are eaten before the kernels swell and should not be pollinated.
plantOut: Plant in late May or early June, after the last frost, once plants are 8 to 15cm tall and have been hardened off. Sweetcorn is wind-pollinated. A single long row pollinates badly and you get cobs with gaps. Plant a block, with plants 34 to 45cm apart each way, so every plant has neighbours.

Do not mix a supersweet variety with an older type nearby. Cross-pollination spoils the extra sweetness. In a cold garden, choose an early variety. Water in dry spells, especially as the flowers open and the cobs swell. Tall plants can rock in the wind. A cane, or a string around the outside of the block, plus a bit of soil mounded at the base, keeps them upright.

spacing.label: Baby corn
spacing.value: 20cm apart, in rows rather than a block

harvest: Cobs start to ripen in late summer. When the silks turn brown, peel a little husk and press a kernel with a fingernail. Watery juice means wait. Creamy juice means pick. Thick, doughy juice means the cob is past its best.

Twist the cob off the stem and cook it soon. The sugar starts turning to starch as soon as it is picked, which is the reason a home-grown cob tastes different from a shop one. For popcorn, leave the cobs to dry on the plant, then finish drying them indoors until the kernels are hard.

problems.title: Gaps in the cob
text: That is poor pollination. Plant in a block, not a row, and do not strip off the tassels. Baby corn is the one type you grow in rows, because you do not want the kernels to swell.

problems.title: Something ate the cobs
text: Birds, mice, squirrels, rats and badgers all take sweetcorn. Sow indoors so mice do not get the seed, and net the plants or bag the cobs once they form.

problems.title: A cool summer
text: Cobs that never ripen were usually sown late, planted in shade, or grown from a late variety in a short season. An early variety, an indoor sowing and a sunny block are the three things that fix that next year.

steps.name: Sow in warmth
steps.text: In mid to late spring, sow 2.5cm deep indoors at about 18 to 21°C.

steps.name: Plant a block after frost
steps.text: In late May or early June, set plants 34 to 45cm apart in a block in full sun.

steps.name: Test a kernel
steps.text: From August, pick when the silks are brown and the juice from a kernel is creamy.

faqs.question: Can I grow sweetcorn in a single row?
answer: You can, but the cobs will be patchy. Pollen has to blow from the tassels onto the silks. A block of at least a few plants each way is what the RHS recommends. Baby corn is the type that is sown in rows.

faqs.question: Is sweetcorn worth growing in the north?
answer: It is more reliable in a long, warm summer, and outdoors it is a gamble in a cold district. Choose an early variety, sow indoors, and use the frost page so you are not planting out in May if your area is an early June garden. A greenhouse or polytunnel removes most of the risk.
